title: Grand Canal of China
summary: China's Grand Canal links Beijing in the north with Hangzhou in the south. The Beijing municipal government dates its origins to 486 BC and gives a length of about 1,797 km, while a China Daily page says Emperor Yang ordered Sui-era work in AD 605–610 and Kublai Khan's canal building ran 1281–1293. It joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014.

uncertainty.note: 486 BC is the origin date per the Beijing government page and the China Daily page (Han Gou waterway); the Sui work is AD 605–610 and the Yuan work 1281–1293. End is the present.

when.display: from 486 BCE; Sui work 605–610 CE; Yuan work 1281–1293; World Heritage 2014

where.modern_name: Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Hangzhou stretch, Zhejiang, China
where.historical_name: Grand Canal (Jing-Hang Da Yunhe), pinned on its Hangzhou stretch

importance.justification: A canal about 1,797 km long that joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014.

reviewer_note: Linear work (model.linear would be true); no model because no opened page gives a canal height or a point to 1 km on the line. Pin is on the Hangzhou stretch, uncertainty 10 km. Lengths differ: Beijing gives about 1,797 km, China Daily gives 3,200 km overall and 2,400 km for the Sui-era canal. Least sure: start year, as the canal was built in sections from 486 BC.
